summary: This bill extends the deadline for TikTok to be sold or banned from 270 days to 540 days by amending section 2(a)(2)(A) of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act.

scores.thoughts: The bill solely extends a regulatory deadline for TikTok divestiture under an existing national security law. It contains no provisions authorizing, increasing, or decreasing any federal expenditures.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation addresses a foreign-controlled social media application and has no connection to health insurance, providers, or medical services.
No references to firearms, background checks, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not alter immigration law, visas, border policy, or pathways to citizenship.
No content related to reproductive health services or abortion access.
No appropriations or policy changes affecting defense budgets or military programs.
The bill contains no environmental, energy, or regulatory provisions concerning climate or natural resources.
No welfare, entitlement, or social assistance programs are addressed.
No education funding, school choice, or federal education policy changes.
No provisions concerning controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
The bill does not modify criminal penalties, sentencing, or policing practices.
While the underlying statute concerns a foreign-owned application, this bill only adjusts the compliance timeline and does not enact tariffs, trade agreements, or new protectionist measures.
No fiscal measures affecting deficits or debt levels are present.
No provisions touching on LGBTQ legal protections or related civil rights.
The legislation does not authorize, modify, or eliminate any foreign assistance programs.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign finance content.
The bill merely extends an existing divestiture deadline under a national-security statute; it neither adds nor removes regulatory oversight of data practices or technology companies.
No labor, union, or employment-law provisions are included.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
